cuetRelevance.pyqFrequency: Core developmental psychology and social work module. Covers ICDS (Anganwadi services), ECCE objectives, juvenile justice, and old-age social welfare schemes.

summary30Seconds: ECCE (Early Childhood Care and Education): Caters to children from birth to 6 years (the crucial brain neurodevelopment window); emphasizes play-based, child-centred learning without formal academic pressure.
Support Services: Creches (for infants and toddlers of working mothers); Day-care centres; Anganwadis under ICDS (Integrated Child Development Services, launched 1975).
Vulnerable Children: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act; Child in Need of Care and Protection (CNCP) vs Child in Conflict with Law (CCL).
Youth & Elderly: National Youth Policy, Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS), National Policy for Older Persons (NPOP), and Old Age Homes.

coreConcepts.title: 1. Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE): Philosophy & Objectives
coreConcepts.content:
Early Childhood spans birth to 8 years, divided into Infancy (0-2 years), Toddlerhood (2-3 years), and Preschool years (3-6 years). Over 85% of cumulative brain development occurs prior to age 6.
Objectives of ECCE:
1. Promote holistic child development across physical, motor, cognitive, socio-emotional, language, and creative domains.
2. Foster curiosity, independence, self-confidence, and social cooperative play.
3. Prepare children smooth transition into primary school without didactic rote-learning.
Key Pedagogical Principles:
- Child-Centred: Activities respect each child's individual developmental pace and cultural context.
- Play-Based Approach: Play is the child's primary medium of learning (Solitary play -> Parallel play -> Associative play -> Cooperative play).
- Experiential and Hands-on: Uses concrete sensory materials (building blocks, clay, water/sand play) rather than formal abstract worksheets.
ncertPointers: NEP 2020 introduces the 5+3+3+4 school structure where the foundational stage comprises 3 years of Anganwadi/Preschool (ages 3-6) and 2 years of primary (ages 6-8).
Jean Piaget's Pre-operational Stage (2-7 years) is characterized by symbolic thought, egocentrism, and animism.

coreConcepts.title: 2. Support Services for Children: Creches, Day Care, and ICDS
coreConcepts.content:
Institutional support systems for early childhood:
1. Creches: Facility providing institutional daycare, supplemental nutrition, sleep/rest, immunizations, and healthcare for infants and young children (6 months to 6 years) of working mothers. Rajiv Gandhi National Creche Scheme (now Palna under Mission Shakti).
2. Day Care Centres: Cater to preschool children for part of the day, offering structured play and socialization.
3. Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS): Launched on October 2, 1975; one of the world's largest community-based early childhood outreach programmes. Delivered through grassroots Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) staffed by Anganwadi Workers (AWW) and Helpers (AWH).
Six Package Services under ICDS:
(1) Supplementary Nutrition, (2) Pre-school Non-formal Education, (3) Nutrition and Health Education, (4) Immunization, (5) Health Check-up, (6) Referral Services.
ncertPointers: Target beneficiaries of ICDS: Children under 6 years, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
Maternity Benefit Act mandates that every establishment employing 50 or more employees must provide an in-house creche facility.

coreConcepts.title: 3. Care and Protection of Vulnerable Children and Youth Programs
coreConcepts.content:
Vulnerable Children: Street children, orphans, abandoned/surrendered children, child labourers, and children affected by HIV/AIDS or abuse.
Legal Framework: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.
Two categories:
- Child in Need of Care and Protection (CNCP): Dealt with by Child Welfare Committees (CWCs) through non-institutional (foster care, adoption through CARA, sponsorship) and institutional mechanisms (Children's Homes, Shelter Homes).
- Child in Conflict with Law (CCL): Minors alleged to have committed an offence; dealt with by the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) through Observation Homes and Special Homes (rehabilitative, not punitive).
Programs for Youth and Elderly:
- Youth (defined as 15-29 years in National Youth Policy): Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS), National Service Scheme (NSS), skill development missions (PMKVY).
- Senior Citizens: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007; Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC) providing financial assistance for running Old Age Homes and Day Care Centres.
ncertPointers: CARA (Central Adoption Resource Authority) is the statutory nodal body for adoption of Indian children.
Childline 1098 is the 24x7 emergency toll-free child helpline service in India.

workedExamples.question: On which historic date was the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) programme officially launched in India, and what is its primary grassroots delivery unit?
solutionSteps: Step 1: The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) was launched on 2nd October 1975 (Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary).
Step 2: It is administered at the village and urban slum level through community Anganwadi Centres (AWCs).
Step 3: An Anganwadi Worker (AWW) and Helper manage each centre.
workedExamples.cuetTip: Launch date: 2nd October 1975. Grassroots centre: Anganwadi. Classic CUET direct question!

workedExamples.question: Two 2-year-old toddlers sit next to each other on a play rug playing with separate toy wooden cars. They observe each other and play with similar toys, but they do not converse or cooperate to build a shared track. According to developmental psychology, what stage of play is this?
solutionSteps: Step 1: In Mildred Parten's stages of play, Solitary play occurs when a child plays alone without noticing others.
Step 2: Parallel play occurs when children play side-by-side with similar toys and mimic each other, but do not directly influence or engage in joint activity.
Step 3: Since the toddlers play alongside with similar cars without active cooperation, it is Parallel Play.
workedExamples.cuetTip: Side-by-side play with similar toys without direct collaboration = Parallel Play (characteristic of 2-3 year old toddlers).

howCuetAsksThis.typicalStem: Which of the following is NOT one of the six package services provided under ICDS?
howCuetAsksThis.strategy: Remember the 6: Supplementary nutrition, non-formal preschool education, immunization, health check-up, referral services, and nutrition/health education.

howCuetAsksThis.typicalStem:
Assertion (A): Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) should strictly avoid formal teaching of reading, writing, and arithmetic through textbooks.
Reason (R): Premature didactic academic pressure causes early school burnout and hinders natural sensorimotor and creative brain development during the critical preschool period.
howCuetAsksThis.strategy: Both are true, and R correctly explains the child-centred play-based philosophy of ECCE.

commonTraps.misconception: Confusing Child Welfare Committee (CWC) with Juvenile Justice Board (JJB).
commonTraps.whyWrong: CWC handles Children in Need of Care and Protection (CNCP - orphans, abandoned); JJB handles Children in Conflict with Law (CCL - minors accused of crimes).
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: CWC = Care and Protection; JJB = Legal Offence adjudication.
commonTraps.trapOptionExample: Sending an orphaned child to the Juvenile Justice Board.

commonTraps.misconception: Believing ICDS provides services only to young children.
commonTraps.whyWrong: ICDS explicitly covers children below 6 years AND pregnant women and lactating mothers.
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: Pregnant and lactating mothers are vital target beneficiaries of ICDS.

practiceQuestions.question: According to neurodevelopmental research highlighted in ECCE, approximately what percentage of cumulative brain development occurs prior to the age of 6 years?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Neuroscience confirms that over 85% of an individual's cumulative brain development takes place before the age of 6, establishing the critical importance of early stimulation.

practiceQuestions.question: Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017 in India, an in-house creche facility is legally mandatory for any establishment employing how many or more workers?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act mandates that every establishment with 50 or more employees must provide a creche facility within a prescribed distance.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following is NOT a target beneficiary group under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme?
practiceQuestions.explanation: ICDS is specifically targeted toward children aged 0-6 years, pregnant women, and nursing/lactating mothers. Senior citizens are covered under distinct social welfare schemes.

practiceQuestions.question: Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2015, which statutory body has the authority to deal with matters concerning a 'Child in Need of Care and Protection' (CNCP)?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Child Welfare Committee (CWC) functions as a bench of magistrates with final authority to dispose of cases related to the care, protection, treatment, and rehabilitation of children in need.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the nationwide 24x7 emergency toll-free phone number for 'Childline' in India, providing assistance to children in distress?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Childline 1098 is India's 24-hour, free, emergency phone service for children in need of aid and assistance.

practiceQuestions.question: Which statutory national body acts as the nodal agency for matters concerning the adoption of Indian children and regulates in-country and inter-country adoptions?
practiceQuestions.explanation: CARA (Central Adoption Resource Authority) is an autonomous statutory body under the Ministry of Women and Child Development mandated to regulate all child adoptions in India.

practiceQuestions.question: In early childhood social play, what type of play involves children playing side-by-side with similar toys and mimicking each other without actively sharing tasks or cooperating on a shared goal?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Parallel play is characteristic of toddlers (approx. 2-3 years) where children play alongside each other using similar toys without direct interaction or joint rules.

practiceQuestions.question:
Assertion (A): Early childhood care programmes should avoid formal didactic instruction such as rote learning of the alphabet and writing on lined paper.
Reason (R): Young children learn most effectively through active sensorimotor play, manipulation of concrete materials, and social peer interactions.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

practiceQuestions.explanation: Both (A) and (R) are true. Didactic formal rote methods run contrary to the natural developmental trajectory of preschool children, which thrives on concrete, play-based exploration.

practiceQuestions.question:
Assertion (A): The Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) handles cases involving abandoned and orphaned children.
Reason (R): Children in Need of Care and Protection (CNCP) are adjudicated by the Child Welfare Committee (CWC), whereas the JJB deals with minors alleged to have committed an offence.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

practiceQuestions.explanation: Assertion (A) is false because abandoned children are handled by the CWC, not the JJB. Reason (R) is true.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match the Social Schemes / Agencies in List I with their Core Mandate in List II:
List I:
(P) ICDS
(Q) CARA
(R) Palna
(S) NYKS

List II:
(1) National creche scheme for children of working mothers
(2) Youth engagement and volunteer rural youth clubs
(3) Grassroots Anganwadi services for 0-6 years and mothers
(4) Central regulatory authority for child adoption
practiceQuestions.explanation: ICDS = Anganwadi services (P-3); CARA = Child adoption authority (Q-4); Palna = National creche scheme (R-1); NYKS = Nehru Yuva Kendra youth clubs (S-2). Matches A.
